turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he could not bear the thought of living without her, that she was his wife and the mother of their son, and that he would do everything in his power to make her last days comfortable and peaceful.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his father that Mother's words had made him feel better, and that he was grateful for all that she had done for him and for the family.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that she had just returned from bringing a warm meal to the eldest son, and that he seemed to be in better spirits after speaking with his mother.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan turned to Wang Lung, her eyes filled with a mix of sadness and determination, and told him that she was glad the eldest son was feeling better after their conversation.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must rest now, and that he would take care of the arrangements for the eldest son's marriage, just as she had wanted.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his father that he was determined to make his mother proud by finding a good wife and settling down soon.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that the eldest son had asked her to help with the preparations for his marriage, and she was unsure of where to begin.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that the eldest son's good spirits after speaking with her made her feel a sense of peace, and that she wanted to see him truly happy before she passed on.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would see to it that the eldest son's marriage was arranged with all due haste, and that she must not worry about it.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told Wang Lung that he would speak with the village matchmaker today and arrange a meeting with the families of several eligible young women.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked Wang Lung if he thought it would be a good idea to start making some traditional wedding clothes for the eldest son's bride, as it was a task that required some time and effort

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the maid to show her the silk that was set aside for the eldest son's bride's wedding clothes

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would send the eldest son to help the maid with the wedding clothes, so that they could be made with the utmost care and attention to detail

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told Wang Lung that he would be happy to help the maid with the wedding clothes, and that he was confident that the bride would be a kind and gentle soul

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid suggested to Wang Lung that it might be better to wait until the eldest son has chosen a bride before starting the wedding clothes

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that it was not just the making of the wedding clothes that was important, but also the choosing of a bride who would bring honor to their family and provide for their son's future

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not have the eldest son choose a bride without his mother's involvement, for she had always been the one to guide him in such matters

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son said to O-lan and Wang Lung that he understood his mother's concern for his future and would do his best to choose a bride who would bring honor to their family

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid told Wang Lung and O-lan that she had heard the eldest son's promise to choose a bride wisely and bring honor to their family, and she was grateful for his consideration

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was glad the eldest son had given his word to choose a bride wisely, but she still worried about the family's future and wanted to ensure that the wedding preparations were started soon

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
